title: Lists, matchups and what players want changed
subtitle: What players wrote about models, themes, matchups and the current rules.
overview: Many answers describe the same problem: a faction has plenty of models, but only a few feel worth taking. On the table, extra activations, hard-to-target models and immunities can leave opponents struggling to respond. Players also praise Bushido’s varied factions, tactical choices and recent errata. Their suggestions focus on specific models, cards and themes.

takeaways.title: A strong list can hide weak models
takeaways.body: Several players say their faction depends on one theme or a few must-take models. Other profiles rarely make the list.

takeaways.title: Extra activations let a player wait out the opponent
takeaways.body: Pass tokens, summons and cheap models let a player save important activations until the opponent has finished. Shooting and camouflage make that late attack harder to answer.

takeaways.title: Some matchups depend on one counter
takeaways.body: Sixth Sense can bypass camouflage; Soulless can stop Fear, poison and OpKi effects. Several players say their faction lacks an affordable answer when its main abilities do not work.

takeaways.title: Players also say the overall game is good
takeaways.body: {{positiveOverall}} answers to the meta-problems question explicitly praise the game overall. They still ask for changes to particular cards, models or lists.

choices.reading: A faction can have many profiles while players keep choosing the same few. Awoken, Jung, Minimoto and Shiho answers name models or themes that feel difficult to leave out.
details: Players describe weak alternatives, expensive support and models that rarely see play.
Ro-Kan raises the opposite concern: a very large selection gives it answers to many opponents.
Compare the usual picks with the models left out, and record whether cost, rules or theme restrictions decide the choice.

theme-value.reading: Players judge themes by which models they allow, what bonuses they give and whether those bonuses help the permitted models. Several answers say strong models can make even a modest theme look strong.
details: Finest Steel is repeatedly praised for keeping the preferred models and adding useful bonuses.
Weak themes are described as restrictive, too situational or too slow to help.
Some bonuses make fragile models playable. Ring of Fire is the recurring example.

matchups.reading: Many answers explain matchups through particular rules: camouflage against Sixth Sense, Fear or poison against immunities, and charges against darkness or Blizzard.
details: Ninja players describe paying for camouflage that some opponents can bypass.
Horse Lords need to reach and hurt their target with the charge.
A second list can cover a bad matchup, but several players feel forced to take one counter-model or a Ronin list.

agency.reading: Players describe models unable to move, target an enemy, pass or take a useful action. Prison is the most repeated example. Waiting, traps and effects with no opposing roll also draw complaints.
details: The frustration is being unable to carry out a plan while models are still on the table.
One Bastions answer criticises Last Stand timing as a surprise an unfamiliar opponent cannot prepare for.
For each disputed effect, ask what the opponent can still do and when they can do it.

tempo.reading: Pass tokens, summons, cheap models and extra activations let a list act after its opponent has committed. Low-model-count lists describe how difficult it is to face that advantage.
details: An extra activation can protect one player’s list while giving the opponent fewer chances to respond.
Several answers link late activations to shooting or fast attackers.
Compare an expensive model’s activations with the cheaper models that could be taken for the same Rice.

balance.reading: Players compare Rice costs, model rules and the best lists each faction can field. Detailed answers point to armour, damage, rerolls, model choice or extra activations as the reason for a rating.
details: Shiho, Horse Lords and Imperial Court are repeatedly named as needing help; Ro-Kan and Ryu are often named as strong.
Other answers call the overall meta good while identifying a few overpowered models or cards.
Suggested changes range from individual profile costs to theme rules and wider faction support.

damage.reading: Shooting and early attacks can remove important models before they contribute. Large models such as Oni and lists with few models are common examples.
details: Players often criticise attacks that combine long reach, high damage and little risk to the attacker.
Other answers value shooting as a way to deal with durable or hard-to-catch models.
Record when the first important model dies, how many activations it loses and whether its side can still score.

resilience.reading: Armour, Rise, healing, high wounds and Last Stand help models survive and hold zones. Opponents describe lacking enough damage or a way to move those models.
details: Minimoto players also name movement, control and displacement as ways to beat their samurai.
Fragile lists describe one failed roll or lost model causing the rest of the list to collapse.
Check the available ways to contest a durable model: damage, displacement, timing and scenario play.

mobility.reading: Movement lets players choose fights, reach support models, avoid slow fighters and keep fragile models safe. A strong melee profile does little if it cannot reach the right fight.
details: Minimoto answers describe opponents avoiding or delaying melee.
Descension players value speed but struggle when their first attack fails to remove a durable target.
Compare movement and placement effects alongside damage: who can engage, disengage or reach the support models?

ki.reading: Some themes provide enough Ki for repeated summons or feats. Other lists struggle to get Ki onto the right models before those models need to act.
details: Hunting Pack and Hozumi are described as providing plenty of Ki.
Awoken and Imperial Court answers describe Ki shortages, expensive support and models unable to keep up with one another.
Follow the turn: who generates Ki, who transfers it, who moves, and when the model can use its feat.

dice.reading: Players criticise Preordain’s dice changes. Players with fragile or low-count lists also describe how one failed roll can decide a game when they lack rerolls.
details: Several answers describe Preordain as a near-mandatory three-Rice purchase.
Effects that work without an opposing roll also draw criticism.
Compare the cost, availability and choices left after a failed roll or a changed result.

scenario.reading: A model or theme needs to help before the important scoring turns. Answers discuss late bonuses, portals, zone-holding and cards that award scenario points.
details: Kinshi and Yurei answers question bonuses that arrive after the most important turns.
Other players describe games ending early through time limits or heavy losses, and ask how remaining points should be awarded.
Compare lists across zones, VIM scenarios and scenarios that require early scoring.

development.reading: Some players praise recent errata. Others say new releases outclass older models, or that sudden changes leave a list without useful replacements.
details: Awoken changes receive both praise and criticism.
Playtesting comments ask for more matchups to be checked before release.
Explain which problem a change should fix, then check whether players use more of the faction’s models afterwards.

rules.reading: Players describe looking through the rulebook, errata, tournament documents, FAQ and Discord to find a ruling. Long cards and unclear interactions make that harder.
details: Several answers ask for current rules in one place.
Other answers identify rules that are difficult to interpret or can be exploited.
A rules index and worked examples would help players find and apply the relevant ruling.

identity.reading: Some players want to use a faction’s own models but feel pushed towards a few strong profiles or a Ronin list. Others think overlapping themes give too little reason to choose between them.
details: Requests include better native models and more useful weaker themes.
Ro-Kan’s large selection is praised for variety and criticised for an unclear faction identity.
Keep list-building choices while giving each theme a clear reason to be taken.

ronin.reading: Some players want tighter Ronin restrictions; others want their faction to have better access. Both views appear in the answers.
details: Hozumi is discussed as a way to bring strong Ronin and extra Ki. Universal cards such as Preordain also make lists more similar.
A Silvermoon answer asks for Ronin access that fits the theme.
Check which models each theme allows and which shared picks repeatedly replace faction models.

access.reading: Players describe the time needed to learn matchups, follow releases and keep up with rules. Some report playing less as the game becomes harder to follow.
details: Small groups give players fewer chances to practise different matchups.
Fragile lists can punish an early mistake before a new player gets much practice.
Separate missing information, a need for practice and a lack of in-faction answers when deciding what would help.

chapters.title: Many models, but few regular picks
chapters.lead: Players repeatedly separate their faction’s best list from the rest of its models.
paragraphs: Awoken answers compare must-take profiles with models that rarely earn their Rice. Jung players ask for cheaper Kaizoku, captains and better support. Shiho players describe relying on Keita. These answers explain why a faction can compete while much of its roster still feels weak.

Theme restrictions can reinforce the same choices. Finest Steel is described as excluding models players would leave out anyway, then improving the models they already want. Other themes exclude useful models for bonuses that do little. The proposed fixes therefore need to consider both model profiles and theme rules.

quote.text: It feels less like your playing against Minimoto than against Finest Steel or less like Facing Jung than the Deep.

chapters.counterpoint: Ring of Fire is described as making vulnerable models playable. Players also praise broad model choice. Keep those benefits in mind when changing a dominant theme.

chapters.title: Waiting can leave the opponent with no reply
chapters.lead: Extra activations and pass tokens decide who must move first.
paragraphs: Several answers describe one side using cheap models, summons or passes until the other side has finished its important activations. Shooting, camouflage and fast attackers can then exploit the remaining activations. The opponent has already spent the actions that could have helped.

Prison draws a related complaint: models remain on the table but cannot move, take a useful action or carry out their plan. One answer asks to allow passing instead of losing the remaining activations. The practical question is what the opponent can still do after the effect is applied.

quote.text: Prison has to go or change the rules that you can at least pass and don't lose all your activations with no valid action to make.

chapters.counterpoint: Extra activations also help some lists function. Minimoto and Oni answers describe the problems of having few models. Compare the advantages with the weaknesses of the list using them.

chapters.title: Some matchups depend on having the right model or rule
chapters.lead: The answers name specific rules that decide whether a list’s usual plan works.
paragraphs: Ninja players describe paying for camouflage, then facing Sixth Sense or other ways around it. Fear and poison lose value against immunities. Horse Lords struggle when darkness, Blizzard or camouflage prevents the charge. These complaints identify which opposing rules stop the list’s main plan.

Minimoto answers describe a different weakness: opponents can avoid slow samurai, remove their activations or move them away from a zone. One matchup answer also stresses that different pairs of lists within the same faction create very different games. Compare actual lists and scenarios when checking these claims.

quote.text: I usually have certain list archetypes in mind that are easier/harder to deal with.

chapters.counterpoint: Several answers describe positioning, practice and winnable uphill matchups. Include those examples when testing claims that a matchup has no answer.

chapters.title: Theme bonuses need to arrive in time to score
chapters.lead: Players judge rules by when they help and which scenarios they suit.
paragraphs: The detailed Kinshi answer discusses portal placement, Void counters and falling behind on points. A Yurei answer says a turn-four bonus arrives too late when turns two and three decide the game. Other theme answers mention VIM restrictions and bonuses triggered by losing models.

Players also report games ending before the final turn because of time limits or heavy losses. Suggestions include shorter scenarios and clearer scoring after a side is tabled. Record which turns are played, when the result becomes clear and which objectives remain in reach.

quote.text: I need the theme bonus to be active during those turns, not on turn 4.

chapters.counterpoint: Durable models are valued for holding zones. Changes to scoring or late bonuses should keep useful scenario roles.

chapters.title: Players want better alternatives and clearer rule changes
chapters.lead: Errata, releases and finding current rules affect what players enjoy fielding.
paragraphs: Some answers praise errata and ask for similar attention to weak models. Others describe nerfs as sudden or too severe after they have invested in a list. Awoken answers show both views: some welcome the Fear changes, while others say useful options disappeared without replacements.

Players also describe searching several documents and Discord for rulings, learning more special rules and trying to keep up with difficult matchups. A few connect this workload to playing less or struggling to grow a local group. Clear change notes, current rules in one place and worked examples would address those complaints.

quote.text: Varied places to have to find rules & rulings

chapters.counterpoint: Positive answers praise community engagement, recent fixes and faction variety. Those are parts of Bushido that players want to keep.

connections.title: Theme restrictions reinforce the usual picks
connections.body: These answers discuss theme bonuses alongside which models are worth taking.

connections.title: Waiting leaves fewer replies
connections.body: These answers connect passes or extra activations with the opponent’s remaining actions.

connections.title: Missing counters force list choices
connections.body: These answers describe must-take models or second lists needed for difficult matchups.

connections.title: Damage depends on the target
connections.body: These answers discuss attacks alongside armour, wounds, healing or fragility.

connections.title: Errata change which models get played
connections.body: These answers discuss releases and changes alongside the models or themes players choose.

connections.title: Finding rules makes learning harder
connections.body: These answers connect scattered or complex rules with the time needed to learn the game.

cases.name: Cult of Yurei
cases.reading: Yurei answers praise debuffs, varied models, healing and returning models. Other passages question Fear against common immunities, expensive profiles and theme bonuses that arrive on turn four. Strong skeleton lists and weaker parts of the roster appear in the same discussion.

cases.name: Horse Lords of Ataka
cases.reading: Horse Lords need the charge to work. Darkness, Blizzard, camouflage and durable targets are repeatedly described as problems. Players ask for more models and ways to keep playing after a charge is prevented or fails.

cases.name: Ito Clan
cases.reading: Ito answers praise speed and poison but describe low wounds, little armour and difficulty damaging durable opponents. Cold Blood is criticised for restrictive recruitment and modest bonuses compared with The Blessed.

cases.name: Jung Pirates
cases.reading: Jung players describe The Deep as the main competitive choice. They ask for cheaper Kaizoku and captains, missing models and better support for other themes. Movement and varied list ideas receive praise, while Fear and low Ki remain common problems.

cases.name: Kinshi Temple
cases.reading: Kinshi answers focus on activation control, OpKi, Void counters and portal survival. A detailed answer prefers Everything and Nothing to Zenith of the Void because it gives more control over counter generation. Early attacks can stop the list getting ready.

cases.name: Minimoto Clan
cases.reading: Opponents describe difficulty damaging Minimoto samurai. Minimoto players describe low numbers, slow movement and trouble with prone, traps and displacement. Finest Steel is repeatedly described as improving the models players already prefer.

cases.name: Prefecture of Ryu
cases.reading: Ryu answers praise extra activations, passes, shooting and reliable melee. Opponents repeatedly criticise being waited out. A detailed Ryu answer also identifies OpKi, prone and mobile opponents as problems.

cases.name: Savage Wave
cases.reading: Savage Wave answers describe different lists: Bakemono bring numbers and summons; Ring of Fire helps Oni survive; large Oni remain vulnerable to shooting and being outactivated. Those builds need separate matchup comparisons.

cases.name: Shadow Wind Clan / Ninja lists
cases.reading: Camouflage is central to ninja lists. Sixth Sense, Blizzard, placement and opponents with more passes can take away that advantage. Some opponents rate ninjas extremely highly; ninja answers stress low model count, failed rolls and the differences between themes.

cases.name: Shiho Clan
cases.reading: Shiho answers describe dependence on Keita, expensive models and too few answers to Fear, OpKi and durable opponents. Open Rebellion needs more models or better bonuses. Crowding enemies for melee advantages can also pull models away from the scenario.

cases.name: Silvermoon Trade Syndicate
cases.reading: Silvermoon answers praise events, control, special attacks and varied models. Durable opponents and limited rerolls can leave it short of damage. One answer describes Malosi as hard to leave out; another asks for more theme-appropriate Ronin access.

cases.name: Temple of Ro-Kan
cases.reading: Ro-Kan’s large model selection receives praise for covering many matchups. Villagers, Bastions, traps and Ki also draw repeated criticism. One own-faction answer asks for the faction to be split; others welcome its variety.

cases.name: The Awoken
cases.reading: Awoken answers ask for better internal balance and less dependence on Fear. Family comments describe Ki shortages and control effects that work awkwardly together. Some players praise recent Fear fixes; others miss options removed by the changes.

cases.name: The Descension
cases.reading: Several Descension answers say prison and Buzenbo make the faction look stronger than its other lists. Other passages praise speed and support while describing fragile models and difficulty finishing durable targets.

cases.name: The Imperial Court
cases.reading: Imperial Court answers praise armour, shooting, cover and model count. They also describe low movement, few counters and missing support. One detailed answer explains how Fangshi, Warden and Bai Qian movement and Ki needs get in each other’s way.

counterpoints.title: Players praise the overall game while asking for fixes
counterpoints.body: Several answers call Bushido good or broadly balanced. They value the tactical choices, different factions and chance to compete with varied lists.

counterpoints.title: Some themes keep vulnerable models playable
counterpoints.body: Ring of Fire is described as doing important work for its models. Check how those models would play after a theme change.

counterpoints.title: Some players want more Ronin access
counterpoints.body: Answers ask both for tighter restrictions and for better access. A Silvermoon player gives examples of Ronin recruitment that would fit a theme.

counterpoints.title: Players disagree about errata
counterpoints.body: Awoken changes receive praise and criticism. Some welcome the fixes; others want replacements for the options they lost.

counterpoints.title: Practice and positioning matter too
counterpoints.body: Several writers mention practice, positioning and the differences between actual lists. Include those details when comparing faction matchups.

actions.title: Compare must-take models with unused alternatives
actions.question: Which models or themes keep being chosen, and why are others left out?
actions.measure: Record both choices, their Rice costs, theme restrictions and the scenarios each can cover.

actions.title: Check what the opponent can still do
actions.question: After extra activations or a control effect takes over, which useful actions remain?
actions.measure: Record passes, activations left and actions prevented. Include late shooting and prison lists.

actions.title: Play the actual list pairings
actions.question: Can a second list or an available model improve the difficult matchup?
actions.measure: Name both lists, scenario and terrain. Check Sixth Sense, immunities, charge prevention and armour.

actions.title: Follow Ki and scoring turn by turn
actions.question: Do support models and theme bonuses help before the important scoring turns?
actions.measure: Record Ki generation and transfers, movement, activations, portal survival, VIM restrictions and the first scoring turn.

actions.title: Check the effect of early losses
actions.question: After losing an important model early, what can the player still do to score?
actions.measure: Record when the model dies, its remaining activations and the surviving ways to contest the scenario.

actions.title: Make current rules easier to find
actions.question: Can a new or returning player find the ruling and understand the change?
actions.measure: Keep a current rules index, short explanations of changes and worked examples of difficult interactions.
